task: Repair packet-consumption semantics: the sender must not pre-write a newly emitted pending packet hash into MISSION_STATE.last_packet_sha256. Preserve last_packet_sha256 as the last successfully consumed inbound packet; pending_packet identifies the unconsumed outbound packet. Add/adjust tests proving B→C can be consumed once by C and a replay is rejected only after consumption. Do not change main or authorization boundaries.
acceptance: Builder identifies and fixes the state update that pre-populates last_packet_sha256 with an unconsumed outbound packet
After emitting a packet, MISSION_STATE.last_packet_sha256 still refers to the last consumed inbound packet while pending_packet refers to the new outbound packet
Recipient can consume the new pending packet exactly once; second consumption is rejected as duplicate
Existing tamper, lease collision, expired lease reclaim, transition, compile and unit tests remain passing
No main write, deployment, Identity Kernel/personality/governance change, or credential handling occurs
Builder returns BUILT_NOT_VERIFIED with evidence to LCR-C
lesson: last_packet_sha256 must mean last successfully consumed inbound packet, not the newest emitted outbound packet; otherwise the next recipient sees the pending packet as an immediate duplicate.
